summary: July meetup recap from KotlinKenya and Android254 hosted at Terra Softworks, featuring a talk on Chronos, a BLE-based smartwatch companion app, and a panel on building products users love. Also flags upcoming DroidCon x FlutterCon Kenya 2026 tickets.

JetBrains' monthly roundup covers Kotlin turning 15, a new public AI-coding-agent benchmark built on 105 real Kotlin repo tasks, and the 2.4.10 release alongside 2.4.20-Beta2's coroutine stack trace recovery, faster klib compilation, and expanded Swift export. Also spotlights Ktor, Koin, and Kermit as a KMP starter trio.
Short clip promoting a longer conference talk on using Kotlin Native for game hacking; the video itself carries no further detail beyond linking to the full presentation.

Android Developers Backstage podcast clip on the history of 'unbundling' the Android toolkit, explaining how decoupling libraries from the OS enabled a shift to code-first, Jetpack Compose-driven workflows for faster iteration.

Google explains the philosophy behind official Android Skills: they're only added for verifiable knowledge gaps in current models, each is validated against evals before release, and stacking too many bloats every prompt's token budget. Recommends the Android Knowledge Base tool over hoarding basic skills.

JetBrains Academy's July digest rounds up new PyCharm/Coursera courses on AI app-building and pandas, plus community news: Kotlin's 15th birthday with free Hyperskill catalog access through October and the full IntelliJ IDEA Conf 2026 program for September 8-9.

JetBrains announces ReSharper 2026.2 now ships a full .NET debugger inside AI-first editors like Cursor, Google Antigravity, Devin Desktop, and Kiro, removing the need for a second IDE window during debugging and test runs. No Kotlin or Android relevance.

August's Java Annotated Monthly digest rounds up Java/JVM news, memory-efficiency tips, and AI-development links, with a dedicated Kotlin Corner pointing to pieces on the Exposed SQL library, the new Kotlin AI benchmark, value semantics, and Kotlin's 15th anniversary.

Interview with a DevSecOps engineer at a kids'-phone company describing how Qodana replaced inconsistent linting across Kotlin, TypeScript, and React repos with unified static analysis, dependency scanning, and CIS/NIST-aligned CI gates.

JetBrains ships a preview VS Code/Cursor extension bringing IntelliJ IDEA's Java and Kotlin language intelligence (navigation, completion, debugging, Gradle/Maven/Bazel support) via LSP, aimed at both manual editing and agentic coding workflows like Claude Code.
JetBrains Academy announces an IDE-integrated pandas course for Python data cleaning and DataFrame work, unrelated to Kotlin or Android development.

Argues that after adopting recent Compose performance wins (pausable composition, real dropShadow calls), remaining jank in production apps traces back to how state is structured and read, not the framework itself. Follow-up to a prior 2024-updates piece.

Roundup of ten Compose changes shipped across BOM 2025.08–2026.04: default pausable composition, the new retain{} API for non-serializable UI state, stable Navigation 3, dropShadow/innerShadow, TextFieldState, autofill/auto-sizing text, Material 3 Expressive, and StandardTestDispatcher-based test APIs.

Explains moving away from passing a single screen-level ViewModel deep into Compose UI trees, instead hoisting state at the route level to keep composables reusable, testable in isolation, and preview-friendly.

Covers testing strategies for Android's App Functions API, which lets apps expose on-device data and actions directly to AI agents instead of relying on generic web search, including how to verify agents call the right function and get correct responses.

Introduces Android's App Functions API, which turns apps into structured, agent-callable data providers so AI agents can invoke app actions directly instead of parsing and navigating the UI like a human user.

CommonsWare's Mark Murphy recounts leaving Wear OS after years on Samsung, TicWatch, and Pixel Watch devices for a Pebble Time 2, citing rePebble's open-source foundation, e-paper always-on display, and lower power draw. He plans to write Pebble apps alongside his Kotlin Multiplatform work.

Ktor 3.5.2 ships fixes for a CIO request-handler coroutine leak on half-closed idle connections, a UTF-8 encoding path that slowed every text response 5-7x, Netty HTTP/2 stream cancellation breaking the whole connection, and RateLimit losing principal access when combined with authentication.

Nightly dev snapshot v1.12.10-alpha01+dev4616 of Compose Multiplatform, bundling matching pre-release coordinates for Material3, Lifecycle 2.11.10-alpha01, and Navigation3 1.2.0-alpha03. No release notes accompany the tag; relevant mainly for teams pinning bleeding-edge builds.

Nightly dev snapshot v1.12.10-alpha01+dev4613 of Compose Multiplatform, pairing the same alpha-line versions of Material3, Lifecycle, and Navigation3 as adjacent builds. A plain version tag with no changelog, useful only for tracking exact snapshot coordinates.

Nightly dev snapshot v1.12.10-alpha01+dev4611 of Compose Multiplatform, again bundling matching alpha builds of Material3, Lifecycle 2.11.10, and Navigation3 1.2.0. Another unreleased-notes internal tag in the ongoing 1.12.10 alpha train.

Nightly dev snapshot v1.12.0-rc01+dev4614 of Compose Multiplatform's core artifact, an unannotated tag in the 1.12.0 release-candidate line with no accompanying notes on what changed since the prior rc build.

Nightly dev snapshot v1.12.10-alpha01+dev4606 of Compose Multiplatform, bundling matching alpha coordinates for Material3, Lifecycle 2.11.10, and Navigation3 1.2.0. A bare version tag with no release notes.
Nightly dev snapshot v1.12.0-rc01+dev4607 of Compose Multiplatform's core artifact, part of the ongoing 1.12.0 release-candidate train with no changelog attached to the tag.

Dev-channel snapshot tag bumping Compose Multiplatform, Material3, Lifecycle 2.11.10-alpha01, and Navigation3 1.2.0-alpha03 artifacts together; no release notes beyond the coordinate list, useful only for pinning bleeding-edge KMP builds.
Another dev-channel snapshot tag for the same Compose Multiplatform, Material3, Lifecycle, and Navigation3 alpha coordinates, roughly two hours after a prior build with no changelog content.
Third same-day dev-channel snapshot bumping Compose Multiplatform, Material3, Lifecycle 2.11.10-alpha01, and Navigation3 1.2.0-alpha03 artifact versions in lockstep; no notable changes documented.
Earliest of a run of dev-channel snapshot tags publishing matching Compose Multiplatform, Material3, Lifecycle, and Navigation3 alpha artifact coordinates for continuous-integration consumption.

Detekt 2.0.0-alpha.6 targets Kotlin 2.4.10, Gradle 9.6.1, and AGP 9.3.1, adds an ignoreSealedClasses option to AbstractClassCanBeInterface, and fixes several false positives/negatives across UnusedPrivateProperty, MissingSuperCall, UseDataClass, and CognitiveComplexMethod rules.

Explains Kotlin 2.4.0's now-Stable context parameters as a compile-time-safe alternative to ThreadLocal for ambient values like tenant IDs and trace IDs, showing how they resolve lexically, compose across call chains, and survive coroutine dispatch without propagation bugs; argues constructor injection still wins for per-instance dependencies.

Argues the standard 16ms frame budget only holds at 60Hz and is nearly double the real 8.3ms budget on 120Hz panels; walks through Choreographer's doFrame source to show "Skipped N frames!" divides jitter by the actual refresh interval and only warns after 30 dropped frames, and covers Android 15's Adaptive Refresh Rate shifting the budget at runtime.

Flutter-specific guide for migrating image_picker usage away from broad storage permissions to Android's Photo Picker to satisfy Google Play policy; not applicable to native Android/Kotlin/KMP development.

Rebuilds the same search-and-filter products screen four ways: MVVM and MVI, each with XML Views and Jetpack Compose. Shows MVVM's independent StateFlow fields forcing manual combine() calls for derived UI state, while MVI's single State object computes conditions like empty-state visibility for free.

Argues MVVM and MVI should be picked per-screen, not as a project-wide rule: MVVM's independent state fields suit small screens but let derived conditions drift out of sync, while MVI's single immutable State object trades upfront boilerplate for predictable, testable reducers on complex stateful screens.
Personal essay about 'reality anxiety' — restlessness after closing social media apps — with no Kotlin, Android, or KMP development content beyond a stray Android tag.
Walks through building a Flipkart-style order-tracking timeline UI in Flutter using the order_tracker package. Flutter/Dart only, with no Kotlin or native Android code.

Explains Google's Target API Level deadline of August 31, 2026: apps not targeting a recent SDK risk losing the ability to publish updates or being less discoverable. Covers bumping compileSdk/targetSdk and common breakage in notifications permissions, scoped storage, background/foreground services, and exact alarms.
Promotes a Crunchyroll MOD APK that bypasses subscription verification to unlock ad-free, full-catalog streaming. A piracy walkthrough, not Kotlin/Android development content.
Installation guide for NetMirror APK, an unofficial sideloaded streaming app, covering unknown-sources setup and common install troubleshooting. No Kotlin/Android development content.
Promotional post for a 'Live Earth Satellite View Maps' navigation app claiming lower battery drain and heat than competing map apps. Marketing copy, not Kotlin/Android development content.

Explains Android's predictive back gesture across Views/Activities, Fragments, and Compose, reducing every surface to the same four callback phases (started, progressed, committed, cancelled) driven by a single progress float. Covers the onBackPressedDispatcher API plus three easy-to-miss gotchas beyond basic wiring.

A personal narrative about choosing Android development in college, moving from XML views to Jetpack Compose, and landing an internship at Physics Wallah. Career-story content with no specific technical concepts, APIs, or code covered.

Part 6 of a KMP series proposes sharing only navigation intent between Android and iOS while keeping NavController and SwiftUI NavigationStack fully native. Uses sealed type-safe destinations and a SharedFlow-based one-time navigation effect emitted from a shared ViewModel instead of raw route strings.
Promotional write-up for a YouTube gaming/tech channel covering BGMI gameplay and generic Android tips-and-tricks. Contains no original Kotlin or Android development material.

Launch announcement for a GPS/AR virtual-pet dinosaur game on Google Play, built solo with RevenueCat monetization. Promises future technical deep-dives on GPS state management but offers no implementation details itself.

Walks through Instagram-style feed architecture (fan-out on write vs. read, cursor-based pagination) and implements it on Android with a Retrofit API, a StateFlow-driven ViewModel, Room offline caching, and a Compose LazyColumn infinite-scroll trigger via snapshotFlow.

A generic listicle comparing Android and iPhone across design, performance, cameras, battery, updates, and price for 2026 buyers. Consumer buying-guide content with no developer-relevant technical detail.

Argues Compose UI state should be hoisted only as far as the nearest shared reader/writer rather than defaulting to a ViewModel, distinguishing transient UI element state from business-rule screen state. Also covers when to use remember versus rememberSaveable for state survival.
Promotional post for the FitPesa app, pitching step-tracking, micro-task games, and P2P dropshipping referrals as ways to earn cash in Africa. No Kotlin, Android, or KMP development content.
Step-by-step guide to running Kali Linux with a GUI on a phone via Termux, proot-distro, and a VNC server. General Linux tooling walkthrough, not Kotlin/Android app development.

A reverse-engineering writeup tracing why a Samsung Galaxy AI settings activity silently closes, following the trail through ADB, logcat, a decompiled Settings APK, and a firmware-level floating-feature flag that disables Native AI. Device/firmware internals investigation, not Kotlin/Android app development.
